sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Supinated Row (also known as the Underhand Barbell Row or Yates Row) is a compound pulling exercise performed with an underhand (palms-up) grip on a barbell.

The supinated grip shifts emphasis onto the lower lats and biceps while allowing greater loading than traditional overhand rows.

Made famous by bodybuilder Dorian Yates, this variation is a staple of back-building programs for developing thickness and width.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Greater lat activation, particularly the lower lats
- Increased biceps recruitment due to supinated grip
- Allows heavier loads than pronated bent-over rows
- Builds back thickness and width
- Improves pulling strength for deadlifts and pull-ups
- Shorter range of motion reduces lower back fatigue
- Enhances grip strength
- Develops rhomboid and mid-trap strength
- More comfortable shoulder position for many lifters

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Latissimus Dorsi, Biceps Brachii

Secondary: Rhomboids, Trapezius (middle/lower), Rear Deltoids, Erector Spinae, Brachialis, Forearms and Grip, Core

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Load the barbell with an appropriate weight.
2. Stand with feet hip-width apart, toes pointed forward.
3. Grip the bar with an underhand (supinated) grip, palms facing up.
4. Hands should be slightly narrower than shoulder-width apart.
5. Bend at the hips and knees while keeping your back flat.
6. Torso should be angled 30-45 degrees from horizontal.
7. Let the bar hang with arms fully extended.
8. Engage your core and set your shoulder blades.

sections.heading: Execution
sections.content:
1. Take a deep breath and brace your core.
2. Pull the barbell toward your lower chest / upper abdomen.
3. Drive your elbows back and down along your sides.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
5. Pause briefly in the contracted position.
6. Lower the bar with control back to full arm extension.
7. Maintain the same torso angle throughout the set.
8. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions with controlled tempo.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Using momentum or jerking the weight up
- Standing too upright (reducing back engagement)
- Rounding the lower back during the pull
- Pulling the bar to the chest instead of lower chest/abdomen
- Not fully extending arms between reps
- Flaring elbows out instead of keeping them close
- Excessive knee bend turning it into a squat-row hybrid
- Looking up and hyperextending the neck
- Using too much weight and losing form

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Olympic Barbell (45 lbs/20 kg)
- Weight Plates (appropriate for your strength level)
- Lifting Platform or Stable Floor Surface
- Optional: Lifting Straps (for grip assistance with heavy loads)
- Optional: Lifting Belt (for heavy sets)
- Optional: Chalk (improves grip)
- Recommended: Flat-soled shoes

sections.heading: Choosing Your Weight
sections.content:
1. Start with lighter weight to master form.
2. Use a weight that allows 8-12 controlled reps.
3. Last reps should be challenging but maintain strict form.
4. Progress gradually - form before load.
5. Use straps if grip fails before back.
6. Warm up with lighter sets before working sets.
7. Avoid ego lifting - the supinated grip can stress biceps.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Stance: Feet hip-width apart, toes forward.
2. Grip: Supinated (underhand), slightly narrower than shoulders.
3. Knees: Bent slightly for stability.
4. Hips: Hinged back, torso angled 30-45 degrees.
5. Spine: Neutral from head to tailbone.
6. Shoulders: Packed down and back.
7. Core: Braced throughout the entire movement.
8. Eyes: Focused on the floor a few feet ahead.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Bentover Barbell Row: Pronated (overhand) grip variation
- Pendlay Row: Bar reset on floor each rep, strict form
- T-Bar Row: Landmine or T-bar apparatus row
- Seal Row: Chest-supported variation for strict form
- Dumbbell Row: Unilateral version with dumbbells
- Chest Supported Row: Removes lower back demand

sections.heading: Row Variations
sections.content:
Supinated Row: Underhand grip, lower lat / bicep emphasis
Pronated Bent-Over Row: Overhand grip, upper back focus
Pendlay Row: Strict row from floor each rep
Yates Row: More upright torso, heavier loads
Single-Arm Dumbbell Row: Unilateral version
Cable Row: Constant tension from cables
Inverted Row: Bodyweight horizontal pull

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Lower Back Pain: Switch to chest-supported row or machine row
Bicep Tendinitis: Use pronated grip or neutral grip instead
Limited Hip Mobility: Use landmine or T-bar row
Grip Issues: Use lifting straps or hook grip
No Barbell: Use dumbbells for similar pattern
Beginner Stage: Start with dumbbell rows to learn the pattern before loading heavy
